meta.methodology: Read framework.md, identified the single bechina edge in torahData.js for reference===207 (id 602: דבור ↔ גבורות, type bechina), and read the full source text torah_207.txt. Scanned all nine lines for explicit bechina language (בְּחִינַת, הוּא בְּחִינַת, הוּא דָּבָר אֶחָד מַמָּשׁ, הוּא בְּעַצְמוֹ, הַיְנוּ בְּחִינַת). Evaluated each candidate relationship for bechina vs. eitza classification. Identified missing bechina edges that belong in Package 2 (Torah she-be'al peh / tzaddik / torat chesed cluster).

additions.description: תורה שבעל פה = צדיק הדור — Oral Torah and the tzaddik of the generation are literally one thing
additions.source_text_ref: Line 8: 'כְּשֶׁמְּדַבְּרִים עַל תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה, אוֹ כְּשֶׁמְּדַבְּרִים עַל הַצַּדִּיק הַדּוֹר בְּעַצְמוֹ, הוּא דָּבָר אֶחָד מַמָּשׁ'
additions.notes: The Rebbe explicitly declares these two to be 'one thing literally' (דָּבָר אֶחָד מַמָּשׁ). This is among the strongest bechina formulas in the corpus — stronger than 'הוּא בְּחִינַת' (which asserts shared nature) because it asserts full ontological identity. The reasoning given is: 'עִקַּר תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה הוּא תָּלוּי בְּצַדִּיק הַדּוֹר' — the essence of Oral Torah IS rooted/dependent on (תָּלוּי בְּ) the tzaddik of the generation. The word תָּלוּי here means the Torah literally hangs/is anchored in the tzaddik — this is not the tzaddik causing or generating the Torah, but the Torah having its existence within/through the tzaddik. They are two names for the same living divine teaching-presence. The Zohar proof (Shekhinah sits between two tzaddikim = Torah she-be'al peh) is cited as mystical validation. This is a foundational bechina that explains the entire practical dynamic of the Torah: harsh speech against Torah she-be'al peh falls on the tzaddik because they ARE the same thing. Without this edge, the Torah's central claim in line 8 is unrepresented in the graph.

additions.description: תלמיד חכם = תורה שבעל פה — the Torah scholar IS himself the Torah
additions.source_text_ref: Line 8: 'הַתַּלְמִיד חָכָם הוּא בְּעַצְמוֹ הַתּוֹרָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (מכות כב:): כַּמָּה טִפְּשָׁאֵי וְכוּ דְּקָיְמִי מִקַּמֵּי אוֹרַיְתָא וְכוּ''
additions.notes: The formula 'הוּא בְּעַצְמוֹ הַתּוֹרָה' (he IS himself the Torah) is one of the clearest possible bechina declarations in the Hebrew: 'הוּא בְּעַצְמוֹ' means 'he himself is' — an identity statement of essence, not of cause or function. The Rebbe does not say 'the scholar studies the Torah' or 'the scholar represents the Torah' but 'the scholar IS the Torah.' The Talmudic proof from Makkot 22b (one should stand before a Torah scroll; how much more so before a Torah scholar, since one who does not stand before the scholar is a fool) functions as the classical rabbinic source for this bechina. This edge belongs in Package 2 alongside the edge between תורה שבעל פה and צדיק הדור. It extends the same identity-cluster from the generation's leader to any accomplished Torah scholar, generalizing the bechina beyond the singular case of the gadol ha-dor.

additions.description: תורה שבעל פה = תורת חסד — the Torah produced from sweetened speech is torat chesed (Torah of lovingkindness)
additions.source_text_ref: Line 9: 'אֲזַי הוּא חוֹזֵר וְעוֹשֶׂה מֵהַדִּבּוּרִים תּוֹרָה... וַאֲזַי עוֹשֶׂה תּוֹרַת חֶסֶד, הַיְנוּ לְלַמֵּד לַאֲחֵרִים, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סוכה מט:) עַל פָּסוּק: וְתוֹרַת חֶסֶד עַל לְשׁוֹנָהּ – זֶה הַלּוֹמֵד עַל מְנָת לְלַמְּדָהּ'
additions.notes: The Talmudic definition cited (Sukkah 49b: 'Torah of lovingkindness = one who studies in order to teach others') is a bechina identity statement: torat chesed IS the mode of Torah that is transmitted outward. The word 'הַיְנוּ' (that is to say / meaning) is a standard bechina formula in Rebbe Nachman's teachings — it introduces an equivalence or further definition. Here: 'he makes torat chesed, הַיְנוּ to teach others' — the torat chesed IS defined as the Torah taught outward. In the context of Torah #207, this is not merely a definition but a structural claim: the Oral Torah that the tzaddik embodies (Package 2) realizes its highest form as torat chesed when he sweetens the harsh gevurot and converts them into outward teaching. The relationship between 'תורה' and 'תורת חסד' here is the same as between תורה שבעל פה and its actualized, transmitted form. Priority is medium (rather than high) because the relationship has a slight eitza coloring — the sweetening action 'produces' torat chesed. However, the Rebbe does not present the sweetening as causing something external to the Torah domain; rather, he reveals what the Torah already IS when fully actualized: torat chesed. The 'הַיְנוּ' connector tips the balance toward bechina.

concepts_in_source_text_not_in_dataset: גבורות קשות (harsh gevurot — the specific, intensified form of divine severities that emerge in times of spiritual crisis; lines 2–7)
דעת (da'at — the sefirah of knowledge; cited in line 1 as the source within which the five gevurot reside before breaking forth through the mouth; lines 1–2)
ה' מוצאות הפה (the five articulatory organs of speech — aleph/glottal, bet/labial, gimel/palatal, dalet/dental, vav/lingual; the five channels through which da'at's gevurot emerge as speech; line 1)
המתקת הגבורות (sweetening of the gevurot / mitigation of harsh divine judgments — the central practice of the Torah; appears throughout)
דן לכף זכות (judging favorably / giving the benefit of the doubt — Method 1 for the tzaddik to sweeten the harsh speech against him; line 5)
מקבל יסורים באהבה (accepting suffering with love — Method 2 for the tzaddik to sweeten the harsh gevurot; line 5)
הסתלקות (passing away / spiritual departure — the ultimate mode of sweetening when the tzaddik lacks power to sweeten during his lifetime; line 6)
בעל שם טוב (the Baal Shem Tov — historical example of the tzaddik on whom harsh gevurot fell; his passing is explained through this Torah's framework; line 7)
שבתי צבי / שצ (the false messianic claimant — referred to as הַשַּׁ"צ יִמַּח שְׁמוֹ; the catalyst for the Sabbatean scholars' harsh speech; line 7)
גדולי הדור ולומדים מופלגים שהטעה אותם (great scholars seduced by the Sha'tz — the 'gedolei ha-dor' who were misled and spoke against Torah she-be'al peh; lines 2, 7)
תורה שבכתב (Written Torah — implicitly contrasted with תורה שבעל פה; not named explicitly but present as the background category against which Oral Torah's dependence on the tzaddik is highlighted)

חסד (chesed / lovingkindness — the direction toward which the tzaddik inclines when he judges favorably, mentioned in line 5 as the mechanism of sweetening; also the quality of torat chesed in line 9)

concepts_examined_and_excluded.reason: Harsh gevurot (קשות = harsh/severe) is an intensification of גבורות (Package 1's node) rather than a separate bechina concept. The Rebbe does not create a new equation for 'harsh gevurot' — he simply specifies that sometimes the gevurot that emerge through speech are at the harsh extreme of the gevurot spectrum. No separate bechina edge proposed. The node גבורות (in Package 1) encompasses its harsh intensification.

Da'at appears in lines 1 and 2 as the sefirah that contains the five gevurot before they emerge through the mouth. In line 1, it is cited as kabbalistic background ('כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּכְּתָבִים, שֶׁהַה' גְּבוּרוֹת שֶׁבַּדַּעַת בּוֹקְעִין וְיוֹצְאִין בְּהַפֶּה'). In line 2, it is cited as the reason why harsh gevurot specifically come through the great sages — they have great da'at. Da'at and gevurot are related here as container-and-contents, not as bechina (parallel aspects of the same thing). The gevurot ARE within the da'at — this is an eitza-like structural relationship (da'at → gives birth to speech through gevurot). However, the Rebbe does not declare 'da'at IS gevurot' or 'da'at IS speech' in this Torah; he uses da'at as the reservoir from which gevurot flow. No bechina edge proposed for this Torah (though other Torahs in the dataset do equate da'at with various concepts).

The sweetening of gevurot is the central EITZA concept of the teaching — it is the practice that transforms the situation. It is not equated with anything via bechina language. The Rebbe describes it as the outcome of Torah study, good speech, judging favorably, and accepting suffering. It is a causal-flow concept (X → המתקה → Y), not a parallel-nature concept. No bechina edge proposed.

The Rebbe describes histalkut (spiritual passing) as a last-resort sweetening mechanism: 'עַל יְדֵי הִסְתַּלְּקוּתוֹ נִשְׁמָתוֹ מַמְתֶּקֶת' — through his passing, his soul sweetens. This is an eitza relationship (histalkut → soul sweetens gevurot), not a bechina. The Rebbe does not declare 'histalkut IS an aspect of gevurot' or 'the soul IS sweetening.' No bechina edge proposed.

In line 5, the Rebbe says that by judging favorably (דן לכף זכות), the tzaddik 'inclines toward chesed' (מַטֶּה כְּלַפֵּי חֶסֶד) and thereby sweetens the gevurot. The relationship between chesed and favorable judgment is evocative of a bechina (judging favorably IS inclining toward chesed), and in other Torahs of Rebbe Nachman such equations appear explicitly. However, in this Torah, the Rebbe uses 'מַטֶּה כְּלַפֵּי' (inclines toward), which is directional language suggesting tendency/causation rather than identity. He is describing an eitza: favorable judgment → chesed-inclination → sweetening. This is not the same as 'judging favorably IS chesed by essential nature.' No bechina edge proposed for this Torah.

concepts_examined_and_excluded.concept: תורת חסד as a node vs. an attribute
concepts_examined_and_excluded.reason: The question arises whether תורת חסד is a standalone node or an attribute/specification of תורה שבעל פה. The analysis treats it as a distinct node (because the Rebbe names it separately and grounds it in its own Talmudic definition from Sukkah 49b), while recognizing that it belongs within Package 2 as a bechina-linked member of the same conceptual family. The proposed bechina edge (תורה שבעל פה ↔ תורת חסד) reflects this membership in the same domain.

analysis_notes.gap_explanation: Torah #207 has one dataset bechina edge (id 602: דבור ↔ גבורות), which correctly captures the Torah's foundational axiom. However, the teaching contains three additional bechina relationships in its second half (lines 8–9) that are entirely absent from the dataset: (1) the explicit identity of Oral Torah with the tzaddik ha-dor ('one thing literally'); (2) the explicit identity of the Torah scholar with the Torah itself ('he IS himself the Torah'); (3) the identity of the fully actualized Oral Torah with torat chesed ('הַיְנוּ limeaned to teach others'). These three missing edges form a second connected package (Package 2) that is currently unrepresented in the graph for Torah #207. The dataset captures the foundational problem (speech = gevurot, requiring sweetening) but misses the resolution (Torah = tzaddik = torat chesed, the domain into which the sweetening flows). Adding these three edges would complete the representation of Torah #207's full argument.
analysis_notes.source_text_summary: Torah #207 is a nine-line teaching explaining the spiritual mechanics of speech as gevurot, the danger of harsh gevurot falling on the tzaddik of the generation, and the tzaddik's two methods for sweetening them. The teaching proceeds: (1) Axiom: all speech is an aspect of gevurot (from Psalm 145 and Kabbalistic writings about the five gevurot of da'at). They need sweetening. (2) Sometimes harsh gevurot emerge through the great sages (because of their great da'at) — they come through the sages' da'at and burst forth as harsh speech. (3) When the sages are in a diminished state (due to sin), they cannot sweeten these gevurot. (4) The unsweetened harsh speech falls on the tzaddik of the generation. (5) The tzaddik can sweeten it by: (a) judging the critics favorably (inclining toward chesed), or (b) accepting the suffering with love. (6) If neither works, he may fall from his level or die (histalkut); and through his passing, his soul sweetens the gevurot. (7) Historical example: the Baal Shem Tov's passing was caused by harsh speech from scholars seduced by Shabbetai Tzvi, who spoke against Oral Torah — that speech fell on the Besht as the gadol ha-dor, and caused two holes in his heart. (8) Theological depth: attacking Oral Torah and attacking the tzaddik ha-dor are the same thing, because Torah she-be'al peh IS rooted in the tzaddik ha-dor (Zohar: Shekhinah between two tzaddikim = Oral Torah); and the talmid chakham IS himself the Torah (Makkot 22b). (9) The positive outcome: when the tzaddik sweetens the speech, he transforms it into Torah — specifically torat chesed (Torah taught to others; Sukkah 49b), sweetening the gevurot through the act of teaching.
